title: Knowledge atom
description: One piece of an expert's knowledge. Channel-neutral: it names no platform, model or audience. Adapters turn atoms into Hatch lessons, Claude agents, prompt packs and the like.

statement.description: The claim, in the expert's own words where possible.

why.description: The reason behind it. Optional in the file, but the quality benchmark requires it on most confirmed atoms.

unless.description: When the rule fails or does not apply.

example.description: The story or evidence behind it.

firm.description: True only when the expert has said outright that this point stands even where common practice in their field differs. The agent then follows it and says it is the expert's deliberate stance.

practice.description: What well-established practice in the expert's field says, when it differs from this point. The agent mentions it alongside the expert's view.

corrects.description: What plain Claude would tell a client instead, in a sentence: the answer this point corrects. The agent uses the contrast; an audit rechecks it when models change.

when.description: The client situation this applies to, in plain words, e.g. first-time landlord, older house, tenant already in.

place.description: Where it holds, when that matters (a country, state or city: rules, suppliers, prices). Empty means anywhere.

domain.description: Areas of the expert's field, e.g. testing, database, security, ux.

applies_to.description: Words in a piece of work that make this relevant. Empty means it applies broadly.

legacy.description: Ids in older stores this came from, e.g. Hatch lesson ids.

source.description: Where it came from, e.g. interview date.

ext.description: Channel-specific data kept so a store can round-trip, namespaced by channel, e.g. ext.hatch = {for, detail, added}. Atoms never depend on it.

evidence.description: Whether this point beats plain Claude, from the edge audit and head-to-head picks.

edge.description: edge: plain Claude does not say it; partial: says part of it; generic: already says it.

note.description: What plain Claude said or missed, in a line.

won.description: Head-to-head scenarios the agent won where this point made the difference.

lost.description: Head-to-head scenarios lost for want of this point.
